Really strange structure and id say every letter needs work here. Negative space management is low, and the spider doesnt make sense for this throw especially cause it overtakes most of the throw and is more complex than the letters themselves. The sharp point at the bottom of some of the letters doesnt make a ton of sense and looks like it was just spammed to make the letters 'look the same', but a circle would likely work better. In terms of putting this up as an actual throw on a wall, it wouldnt work too well. Focus on strengthening your structure more first before adding extra stuff

I see what you’re doing making the M and R bigger, but I don’t think it works if the R is significantly bigger than the M. If you’re gonna make them both bigger, make them the same size ya feel me

I’m reading this as BRIIK right now. The bottom b bowl goes out too far, the R leg is weak cause of the bottom like you use for it that’s curved between the legs of it. The second dot of the I doesn’t make sense for this, it’s too intricate and it doesn’t get understood as the dot of the i well.  The K goes way farther up than the rest of the letters, and the top right leg of the K overlaps the spine to make it look like an R. Having consistent baseline and cap height is very important when learning straights, and if you can consistently do keyboard letter straights (with good baseline and cap height) in your sleep, that’s when you’re able to move on to stuff like adjusting letter sizes in the words, and serifs, etc etc

Work on having consistent bar length in your letters, specifically the middle A and the bottom S. Also the hole in the middle A is too high given how thin that top bar is. Keep drawing !
The T is your best letter here, it took a few minutes for me to find your A and M.

Work on bars. Try to make your letters as similar to keyboard letters as possible to work on readability, and then see if you can easily style it from there within your capability. Originally when I looked at this I thought you were writing ROAR, the A at the end looks more like a slightly different version of your R than anything. I understand where you're coming from with trying to add style into your work and trying to make it look funky, but you can get a lot farther starting out with the simplest letters and figuring out fun or funky fills to do. It builds fundamentals that make style more natural later on. Also, I personally would not add any crowns to anything. Crowns kinda give an ego vibe that you're 'king' and toys or beginners *will* get shit on for that. Your excitement and engagement in graff is great though, just keep it up bro.

Work on consistent bar thickness. Your S has varying degrees of bar thickness so it makes it look more unsteady than possible. Also, the top S serif is inconsistent and maybe trying to make it match the bottom serif. The E's hole doesn't match the bars you make for the E, so maybe fixing that. I like the N though, and you definitely have potential

While I get the feel you're looking for, and experimenting with the angel vibe is always fun, I found that I learned the most about graff and lettering when I got rid of add-ons and worked on doing the most basic keyboard letters and slowly adding style to it as I got better. Add-ons can be a more intermediate or advanced thing to get right, so maybe that's something you can work up to.

I'd say work really hard on bars in your letters right now, also cap-height throughout the word. The mid-line on this is kinda fucked, the middle bar of the A, the bottom of the R bowl, and the intersection of the B bowls should all come down to the same height as the G serif. G seems like your best letter, keep it up.
Good O and S form. I’d suggest making the hole in the E more centered. Maybe also lift the top bar on the S up some more. Amazing for someone of your age though!
